prompt: Implement a type-safe heterogeneous container: TypedSettings stores one value per Class key in a Map<Class<?>, Object> and returns it already typed via type.cast, so callers never write a cast of their own.
explanation: A normal generic container fixes one element type, but here the type parameter lives on the METHODS, so each put/get pair is checked independently and the map itself can hold mixed values. The Class<T> argument is a type token: it carries T at run time, so type.cast(values.get(type)) converts Object back to T with a real check instead of an unchecked cast. Rejecting a null key matters because null cannot cast anything, which would silently break the guarantee the container is selling.
hints: The map is declared Map<Class<?>, Object>; only put and get know the specific T, and they get it from the Class<T> parameter.
Class has an instance method cast(Object) that returns T -- use it instead of writing (T) yourself so the check is real.
getOrDefault can just call your own get and swap in the fallback when the result is null.
